scope: Deuteronomy 27–34, all 266 public verses. Prior revisions remain unchanged.

source.verse_hash_method: SHA-256 of the exact original XML verse substring, including written/read notes, not a normalized substitute.
source.public_versification_note: Public Deuteronomy 29:1 binds Hebrew 28:69; public 29:2–29 binds Hebrew 29:1–28. All other public verses in chapters 27–34 align directly. All 266 original XML records, including written/read and numbering notes, are hashed in full.

delta_method: F0 retained wording; F1 lexical; F2 syntax/idiom; F3 consequential interpretive, textual, social, or versification choice. Editorial assessments are separate from similarity scores. Independent review has not occurred.

verses.rationale: Preserves the collective speakers and singular first-person command within their address.
verses.before: Moses and the elders of Israel commanded the people, saying, “Keep all the commandment that I command you today.
verses.after: Moses and Israel’s elders gave the people this command: “Keep every commandment I am giving you today.
verses.tsw_comparator: Moses and the elders of Israel commanded the people, saying, “Keep all the commandment that I command you today.

verses.rationale: Keeps crossing-day timing and the two distinct stone preparations.
verses.before: And on the day you cross the Jordan into the land that the LORD your God is giving you, you will set up for yourself large stones and plaster them with plaster.
verses.after: On the day you cross the Jordan into the land the LORD your God is giving you, set up large stones and coat them with plaster.
verses.tsw_comparator: And on the day you cross the Jordan into the land that the LORD your God is giving you, you shall set up for yourself large stones and plaster them with plaster.

verses.rationale: Retains all the instruction, the purpose clause, and the ancestral promise rather than shortening the repetition.
verses.before: You will write upon them all the words of this instruction when you cross over, so that you may enter the land that the LORD your God is giving you, a land flowing with milk and honey, as the LORD, the God of your ancestors, spoke to you.
verses.after: Write all the words of this instruction on them when you cross over, so that you may enter the land the LORD your God is giving you—a land flowing with milk and honey, as the LORD, the God of your ancestors, promised you.
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall write upon them all the words of this instruction when you cross over, so that you may enter the land that the LORD your God is giving you, a land flowing with milk and honey, as the LORD, the God of your ancestors, spoke to you.

verses.rationale: Follows pinned Ebal and repeats plastering; does not substitute the Samaritan location.
verses.before: And when you cross the Jordan, you will set up these stones concerning which I command you today on Mount Ebal, and you will plaster them with plaster.
verses.after: When you have crossed the Jordan, set up these stones on Mount Ebal, as I command you today, and coat them with plaster.
verses.tsw_comparator: And when you cross the Jordan, you shall set up these stones concerning which I command you today on Mount Ebal, and you shall plaster them with plaster.

verses.rationale: Makes the iron prohibition apply to the stones without broadening it to every material.
verses.before: “You will build there an altar to the LORD your God, an altar of stones. You will not wield an iron tool upon them.
verses.after: Build an altar there to the LORD your God, an altar of stones. Do not use an iron tool on them.
verses.tsw_comparator: “You shall build there an altar to the LORD your God, an altar of stones. You shall not wield an iron tool upon them.

verses.rationale: Renders whole stones as uncut in the context of the iron-tool prohibition.
verses.before: You will build the altar of the LORD your God with whole stones and offer burnt offerings upon it to the LORD your God.
verses.after: Build the altar of the LORD your God with uncut stones, and offer burnt offerings on it to the LORD your God.
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall build the altar of the LORD your God with whole stones and offer burnt offerings upon it to the LORD your God.

verses.rationale: Keeps sacrifice, eating, and rejoicing as coordinated actions.
verses.before: You will sacrifice offerings of well-being and eat there and rejoice before the LORD your God.
verses.after: Offer well-being sacrifices there, eat, and rejoice in the presence of the LORD your God.
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall sacrifice offerings of well-being and eat there and rejoice before the LORD your God.

verses.rationale: Preserves the comprehensive inscription and emphasis on clarity.
verses.before: You will write upon the stones all the words of this instruction very clearly.”
verses.after: Write all the words of this instruction on the stones, very clearly.”
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall write upon the stones all the words of this instruction very clearly.”

verses.rationale: Marks the new speakers and the declaration of present covenant identity.
verses.before: Moses and the Levitical priests spoke to all Israel, saying, “Be silent and hear, Israel. This day you have become the people of the LORD your God.
verses.after: Then Moses and the Levitical priests said to all Israel, “Be still and listen, Israel! Today you have become the people of the LORD your God.
verses.tsw_comparator: Moses and the Levitical priests spoke to all Israel, saying, “Be silent and hear, Israel. This day you have become the people of the LORD your God.

verses.rationale: Links listening with enacted obedience while keeping the two legal terms.
verses.before: You will listen to the voice of the LORD your God and do his commandments and his statutes that I command you today.”
verses.after: Listen to the LORD your God and keep his commandments and statutes, which I am giving you today.”
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall listen to the voice of the LORD your God and do his commandments and his statutes that I command you today.”

verses.rationale: Provides the narrative introduction to the mountain ceremony.
verses.before: Moses commanded the people on that day, saying,
verses.after: That day Moses commanded the people:
verses.tsw_comparator: Moses commanded the people on that day, saying,

verses.rationale: Preserves the six names and their assignment to blessing on Gerizim.
verses.before: “These will stand to bless the people on Mount Gerizim when you cross the Jordan: Simeon, Levi, Judah, Issachar, Joseph, and Benjamin.
verses.after: “After you cross the Jordan, these tribes are to stand on Mount Gerizim to bless the people: Simeon, Levi, Judah, Issachar, Joseph, and Benjamin.
verses.tsw_comparator: “These shall stand to bless the people on Mount Gerizim when you cross the Jordan: Simeon, Levi, Judah, Issachar, Joseph, and Benjamin.

verses.rationale: Preserves the other six names and the contrasting mountain assignment.
verses.before: And these will stand for the curse on Mount Ebal: Reuben, Gad, Asher, Zebulun, Dan, and Naphtali.
verses.after: These are to stand on Mount Ebal for the curse: Reuben, Gad, Asher, Zebulun, Dan, and Naphtali.
verses.tsw_comparator: And these shall stand for the curse on Mount Ebal: Reuben, Gad, Asher, Zebulun, Dan, and Naphtali.

verses.rationale: Keeps the specified male audience and loud public delivery.
verses.before: “The Levites will answer and say to every man of Israel with a loud voice:
verses.after: The Levites are to speak loudly to all the men of Israel:
verses.tsw_comparator: “The Levites shall answer and say to every man of Israel with a loud voice:

verses.rationale: Retains both image types, secret placement, and the full congregational response.
verses.before: ‘Cursed is the man who makes a carved or cast image, a detestable thing to the LORD, the work of a craftsman’s hands, and sets it up in secret.’ And all the people will answer and say, ‘Amen.’
verses.after: ‘Cursed is anyone who makes a carved or cast image—something the LORD detests, the work of a craftsman—and sets it up in secret.’ All the people are to answer, ‘Amen!’
verses.tsw_comparator: ‘Cursed is the man who makes a carved or cast image, a detestable thing to the LORD, the work of a craftsman’s hands, and sets it up in secret.’ And all the people shall answer and say, ‘Amen.’

verses.rationale: Renders making light of a parent as dishonoring and retains the response.
verses.before: ‘Cursed is the one who treats his father or mother with contempt.’ And all the people will say, ‘Amen.’
verses.after: ‘Cursed is anyone who dishonors father or mother.’ All the people are to say, ‘Amen!’
verses.tsw_comparator: ‘Cursed is the one who treats his father or mother with contempt.’ And all the people shall say, ‘Amen.’

verses.rationale: Makes the land-boundary action concrete without adding motive.
verses.before: ‘Cursed is the one who moves his neighbor’s boundary marker.’ And all the people will say, ‘Amen.’
verses.after: ‘Cursed is anyone who moves a neighbor’s boundary marker.’ All the people are to say, ‘Amen!’
verses.tsw_comparator: ‘Cursed is the one who moves his neighbor’s boundary marker.’ And all the people shall say, ‘Amen.’

verses.rationale: Keeps the literal vulnerable traveler and deliberate misdirection.
verses.before: ‘Cursed is the one who causes a blind person to wander on the road.’ And all the people will say, ‘Amen.’
verses.after: ‘Cursed is anyone who leads a blind person astray on the road.’ All the people are to say, ‘Amen!’
verses.tsw_comparator: ‘Cursed is the one who causes a blind person to wander on the road.’ And all the people shall say, ‘Amen.’

verses.rationale: Preserves each protected group and the judicial wrong.
verses.before: ‘Cursed is the one who distorts the justice due to the resident alien, orphan, and widow.’ And all the people will say, ‘Amen.’
verses.after: ‘Cursed is anyone who denies justice to a resident foreigner, a fatherless child, or a widow.’ All the people are to say, ‘Amen!’
verses.tsw_comparator: ‘Cursed is the one who distorts the justice due to the resident alien, orphan, and widow.’ And all the people shall say, ‘Amen.’

verses.rationale: States the sexual act plainly while retaining the covering image for explanation in a note. Consistency refinement: Uses garment for the same uncovering-the-father’s-kanaph expression already retained in public 22:30. This makes the recurring sexual-marital image recognizable without removing it or changing the prohibited relationship.
verses.before: ‘Cursed is the one who lies with his father’s wife, because he has uncovered his father’s skirt.’ And all the people will say, ‘Amen.’
verses.after: ‘Cursed is anyone who has sex with his father’s wife, for he has uncovered his father’s garment.’ All the people are to say, ‘Amen!’
verses.tsw_comparator: ‘Cursed is the one who lies with his father’s wife, because he has uncovered his father’s skirt.’ And all the people shall say, ‘Amen.’

consistency_history.prior_after: ‘Cursed is anyone who has sex with his father’s wife, for he has uncovered his father’s covering.’ All the people are to say, ‘Amen!’
consistency_history.prior_rationale: States the sexual act plainly while retaining the covering image for explanation in a note.
consistency_history.rationale: Uses garment for the same uncovering-the-father’s-kanaph expression already retained in public 22:30. This makes the recurring sexual-marital image recognizable without removing it or changing the prohibited relationship.

verses.rationale: Keeps the comprehensive animal prohibition without euphemism.
verses.before: ‘Cursed is the one who lies with any animal.’ And all the people will say, ‘Amen.’
verses.after: ‘Cursed is anyone who has sex with any animal.’ All the people are to say, ‘Amen!’
verses.tsw_comparator: ‘Cursed is the one who lies with any animal.’ And all the people shall say, ‘Amen.’

verses.rationale: Preserves both paternal and maternal relationships.
verses.before: ‘Cursed is the one who lies with his sister, the daughter of his father or the daughter of his mother.’ And all the people will say, ‘Amen.’
verses.after: ‘Cursed is anyone who has sex with his sister, whether his father’s daughter or his mother’s daughter.’ All the people are to say, ‘Amen!’
verses.tsw_comparator: ‘Cursed is the one who lies with his sister, the daughter of his father or the daughter of his mother.’ And all the people shall say, ‘Amen.’

verses.rationale: Names the relationship directly and keeps the repeated assent.
verses.before: ‘Cursed is the one who lies with his mother-in-law.’ And all the people will say, ‘Amen.’
verses.after: ‘Cursed is anyone who has sex with his mother-in-law.’ All the people are to say, ‘Amen!’
verses.tsw_comparator: ‘Cursed is the one who lies with his mother-in-law.’ And all the people shall say, ‘Amen.’

verses.rationale: Retains the lethal force of striking down in context without adding a specific weapon.
verses.before: ‘Cursed is the one who strikes his neighbor in secret.’ And all the people will say, ‘Amen.’
verses.after: ‘Cursed is anyone who strikes down a neighbor in secret.’ All the people are to say, ‘Amen!’
verses.tsw_comparator: ‘Cursed is the one who strikes his neighbor in secret.’ And all the people shall say, ‘Amen.’

verses.rationale: Makes innocent blood refer to the person killed and preserves bribery.
verses.before: ‘Cursed is the one who takes a bribe to strike an innocent life.’ And all the people will say, ‘Amen.’
verses.after: ‘Cursed is anyone who accepts a bribe to kill an innocent person.’ All the people are to say, ‘Amen!’
verses.tsw_comparator: ‘Cursed is the one who takes a bribe to strike an innocent life.’ And all the people shall say, ‘Amen.’

verses.rationale: Keeps doing as the meaning of upholding and closes the ceremonial address.
verses.before: ‘Cursed is the one who does not establish the words of this instruction by doing them.’ And all the people will say, ‘Amen.’
verses.after: ‘Cursed is anyone who does not uphold the words of this instruction by carrying them out.’ All the people are to say, ‘Amen!’”
verses.tsw_comparator: ‘Cursed is the one who does not establish the words of this instruction by doing them.’ And all the people shall say, ‘Amen.’

verses.rationale: Keeps the emphatic listening condition and the full scope of commandments and nations.
verses.before: “And it will be, if you diligently listen to the voice of the LORD your God, being careful to do all his commandments that I command you today, then the LORD your God will set you high above all the nations of the earth.
verses.after: “If you listen carefully to the LORD your God and faithfully carry out all his commandments that I am giving you today, the LORD your God will set you high above all the nations of the earth.
verses.tsw_comparator: “And it will be, if you diligently listen to the voice of the LORD your God, being careful to do all his commandments that I command you today, then the LORD your God will set you high above all the nations of the earth.

verses.rationale: Retains overtaking as the recurring image that will also describe curses.
verses.before: All these blessings will come upon you and overtake you if you listen to the voice of the LORD your God.
verses.after: All these blessings will come upon you and overtake you, if you listen to the LORD your God.
verses.tsw_comparator: All these blessings will come upon you and overtake you if you listen to the voice of the LORD your God.

verses.rationale: Keeps the two settings in a parallel blessing line.
verses.before: Blessed will you be in the city, and blessed will you be in the field.
verses.after: You will be blessed in the town and blessed in the fields.
verses.tsw_comparator: Blessed shall you be in the city, and blessed shall you be in the field.

verses.rationale: Retains the repeated fruit image and the specified animal offspring.
verses.before: Blessed will be the fruit of your womb, the fruit of your ground, and the fruit of your livestock, the offspring of your cattle and the increase of your flock.
verses.after: Blessed will be the fruit of your womb, the fruit of your ground, and the fruit of your livestock— the calves of your herds and the young of your flocks.
verses.tsw_comparator: Blessed shall be the fruit of your womb, the fruit of your ground, and the fruit of your livestock, the offspring of your cattle and the increase of your flock.

verses.rationale: Preserves both household food containers rather than generalizing to prosperity.
verses.before: Blessed will be your basket and your kneading bowl.
verses.after: Your basket and your kneading bowl will be blessed.
verses.tsw_comparator: Blessed shall be your basket and your kneading bowl.

verses.rationale: Keeps the paired movement formula that recurs in the curses.
verses.before: Blessed will you be when you come in, and blessed will you be when you go out.
verses.after: You will be blessed when you come in and blessed when you go out.
verses.tsw_comparator: Blessed shall you be when you come in, and blessed shall you be when you go out.

verses.rationale: Preserves the one/seven contrast and divine agency in defeat.
verses.before: “The LORD will cause your enemies who rise against you to be struck down before you. They will come out against you one way and flee before you seven ways.
verses.after: The LORD will cause the enemies who rise against you to be defeated before you. They will come against you along one road and flee from you along seven.
verses.tsw_comparator: “The LORD will cause your enemies who rise against you to be struck down before you. They will come out against you one way and flee before you seven ways.

verses.rationale: Retains commanded blessing, stored produce, work, and land.
verses.before: The LORD will command the blessing upon you in your barns and in all to which you put your hand, and he will bless you in the land that the LORD your God is giving you.
verses.after: The LORD will command blessing upon your storehouses and everything you undertake. He will bless you in the land the LORD your God is giving you.
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD will command the blessing upon you in your barns and in all to which you put your hand, and he will bless you in the land that the LORD your God is giving you.

verses.rationale: Keeps holiness, oath, and the continuing obedience condition together.
verses.before: The LORD will establish you as a holy people for himself, as he swore to you, if you keep the commandments of the LORD your God and walk in his ways.
verses.after: The LORD will establish you as a people holy to himself, as he swore to you, if you keep the commandments of the LORD your God and walk in his ways.
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD will establish you as a holy people for himself, as he swore to you, if you keep the commandments of the LORD your God and walk in his ways.

verses.rationale: Preserves the name-called-over image instead of replacing it solely with ownership language.
verses.before: Then all the peoples of the earth will see that the name of the LORD is called upon you, and they will fear you.
verses.after: All the peoples of the earth will see that the LORD’s name is called over you, and they will fear you.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then all the peoples of the earth will see that the name of the LORD is called upon you, and they will fear you.

verses.rationale: Keeps this verse’s womb/livestock/ground order and repeated ancestral oath.
verses.before: The LORD will make you abound in good—in the fruit of your womb, the fruit of your livestock, and the fruit of your ground—upon the ground that the LORD swore to your ancestors to give you.
verses.after: The LORD will give you abundance—in the fruit of your womb, the fruit of your livestock, and the fruit of your ground—in the land the LORD swore to your ancestors to give you.
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD will make you abound in good—in the fruit of your womb, the fruit of your livestock, and the fruit of your ground—upon the ground that the LORD swore to your ancestors to give you.

verses.rationale: Preserves the heavenly storehouse, seasonal rain, and asymmetric lending promise.
verses.before: The LORD will open for you his good treasury, the heavens, to give rain to your land in its season and to bless all the work of your hand. You will lend to many nations, but you will not borrow.
verses.after: The LORD will open his good storehouse, the heavens, to give your land rain in its season and bless all the work of your hands. You will lend to many nations, but you will not borrow.
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD will open for you his good treasury, the heavens, to give rain to your land in its season and to bless all the work of your hand. You will lend to many nations, but you will not borrow.

verses.rationale: Retains the paired bodily and vertical images with their explicit condition.
verses.before: The LORD will make you the head and not the tail, and you will be only above and not below, if you listen to the commandments of the LORD your God that I command you today, being careful to do them,
verses.after: The LORD will make you the head, not the tail. You will be above, never below, if you listen to the commandments of the LORD your God that I am giving you today and faithfully carry them out.
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD will make you the head and not the tail, and you will be only above and not below, if you listen to the commandments of the LORD your God that I command you today, being careful to do them,

verses.rationale: Keeps the directional image and specifies the departure as service to other gods.
verses.before: and do not turn aside from any of the words that I command you today, to the right or to the left, to go after other gods to serve them.
verses.after: Do not turn aside, to the right or to the left, from any of the words I command you today by following other gods and serving them.
verses.tsw_comparator: and do not turn aside from any of the words that I command you today, to the right or to the left, to go after other gods to serve them.

verses.rationale: Matches the blessing introduction while preserving the added statutes and negative condition.
verses.before: “But it will be, if you do not listen to the voice of the LORD your God, being careful to do all his commandments and statutes that I command you today, then all these curses will come upon you and overtake you.
verses.after: But if you do not listen to the LORD your God and faithfully carry out all his commandments and statutes that I am giving you today, all these curses will come upon you and overtake you.
verses.tsw_comparator: “But it will be, if you do not listen to the voice of the LORD your God, being careful to do all his commandments and statutes that I command you today, then all these curses will come upon you and overtake you.

verses.rationale: Retains the exact reversal of the town/field blessing pattern.
verses.before: Cursed will you be in the city, and cursed will you be in the field.
verses.after: You will be cursed in the town and cursed in the fields.
verses.tsw_comparator: Cursed shall you be in the city, and cursed shall you be in the field.

verses.rationale: Keeps both containers and their direct reversal.
verses.before: Cursed will be your basket and your kneading bowl.
verses.after: Your basket and your kneading bowl will be cursed.
verses.tsw_comparator: Cursed shall be your basket and your kneading bowl.

verses.rationale: Follows this verse’s list without importing the additional generic livestock phrase from verse 4.
verses.before: Cursed will be the fruit of your womb, the fruit of your ground, the offspring of your cattle and the increase of your flock.
verses.after: Cursed will be the fruit of your womb and the fruit of your ground, the calves of your herds and the young of your flocks.
verses.tsw_comparator: Cursed shall be the fruit of your womb, the fruit of your ground, the offspring of your cattle and the increase of your flock.

verses.rationale: Preserves the repeated movement formula under the curse.
verses.before: Cursed will you be when you come in, and cursed will you be when you go out.
verses.after: You will be cursed when you come in and cursed when you go out.
verses.tsw_comparator: Cursed shall you be when you come in, and cursed shall you be when you go out.

verses.rationale: Keeps the unannounced shift to divine first person rather than harmonizing me to him.
verses.before: “The LORD will send upon you curse, confusion, and rebuke in all to which you put your hand to do, until you are destroyed and perish quickly because of the evil of your deeds, because you have abandoned me.
verses.after: The LORD will send curse, confusion, and rebuke upon everything you undertake, until you are destroyed and quickly perish because of your evil deeds in forsaking me.
verses.tsw_comparator: “The LORD will send upon you curse, confusion, and rebuke in all to which you put your hand to do, until you are destroyed and perish quickly because of the evil of your deeds, because you have abandoned me.

verses.rationale: Retains clinging disease and removal from the land.
verses.before: The LORD will make plague cling to you until he has finished you from the ground that you are entering to possess.
verses.after: The LORD will make pestilence cling to you until he has consumed you from the land you are entering to possess.
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD will make plague cling to you until he has finished you from the ground that you are entering to possess.

verses.rationale: Follows the pinned sword reading among difficult affliction terms and retains all seven items.
verses.before: The LORD will strike you with wasting disease, fever, inflammation, burning heat, drought, blight, and mildew, and they will pursue you until you perish.
verses.after: The LORD will strike you with wasting disease, fever, inflammation, scorching heat, sword, blight, and mildew. They will pursue you until you perish.
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD will strike you with wasting disease, fever, inflammation, burning heat, drought, blight, and mildew, and they will pursue you until you perish.

verses.rationale: Preserves the metal images without replacing them with an explanatory drought paraphrase.
verses.before: The heavens over your head will be bronze, and the earth beneath you iron.
verses.after: The sky over your head will be bronze, and the earth beneath you will be iron.
verses.tsw_comparator: The heavens over your head will be bronze, and the earth beneath you iron.

verses.rationale: Keeps rain transformed into dust and its downward movement.
verses.before: The LORD will make the rain of your land powder and dust; from the heavens it will come down upon you until you are destroyed.
verses.after: The LORD will turn your land’s rain into dust and powder. It will fall on you from the heavens until you are destroyed.
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD will make the rain of your land powder and dust; from the heavens it will come down upon you until you are destroyed.

verses.rationale: Retains the numerical reversal and the ensuing public horror.
verses.before: “The LORD will cause you to be struck down before your enemies. You will go out against them one way and flee before them seven ways, and you will become a horror to all the kingdoms of the earth.
verses.after: The LORD will cause you to be defeated before your enemies. You will go against them along one road and flee from them along seven. You will become an object of horror to all the kingdoms of the earth.
verses.tsw_comparator: “The LORD will cause you to be struck down before your enemies. You will go out against them one way and flee before them seven ways, and you will become a horror to all the kingdoms of the earth.

verses.rationale: Preserves exposed bodies and the absence of anyone protecting them.
verses.before: Your dead body will become food for every bird of the heavens and animal of the earth, and there will be no one to frighten them away.
verses.after: Your corpses will become food for all the birds of the heavens and the animals of the earth, with no one to frighten them away.
verses.tsw_comparator: Your dead body will become food for every bird of the heavens and animal of the earth, and there will be no one to frighten them away.

verses.rationale: Uses the recorded read form for hemorrhoids, with the written tumor term documented in a note.
verses.before: The LORD will strike you with the boils of Egypt, tumors, scabs, and itching, from which you cannot be healed.
verses.after: The LORD will strike you with the boils of Egypt, hemorrhoids, scabs, and itching, from which you cannot be healed.
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD will strike you with the boils of Egypt, tumors, scabs, and itching, from which you cannot be healed.

verses.rationale: Retains three afflictions and the heart as the seat of understanding.
verses.before: The LORD will strike you with madness, blindness, and confusion of heart.
verses.after: The LORD will strike you with madness, blindness, and a bewildered heart.
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD will strike you with madness, blindness, and confusion of heart.

verses.rationale: Keeps the noon/darkness contrast and repeated absence of rescue.
verses.before: You will grope at noon as the blind person gropes in darkness, and you will not make your ways prosper. You will only be oppressed and robbed all the days, with no one to save you.
verses.after: At noon you will grope about like a blind person groping in darkness, and you will have no success in your ways. You will be oppressed and robbed continually, with no one to rescue you.
verses.tsw_comparator: You will grope at noon as the blind person gropes in darkness, and you will not make your ways prosper. You will only be oppressed and robbed all the days, with no one to save you.

verses.rationale: Preserves sexual violence in the written verb rather than allowing the euphemistic read form to obscure harm.
verses.before: “You will betroth a woman, but another man will lie with her. You will build a house, but you will not live in it. You will plant a vineyard, but you will not begin to enjoy its fruit.
verses.after: You will be engaged to a woman, but another man will rape her. You will build a house but never live in it. You will plant a vineyard but never enjoy its fruit.
verses.tsw_comparator: “You will betroth a woman, but another man will lie with her. You will build a house, but you will not live in it. You will plant a vineyard, but you will not begin to enjoy its fruit.

verses.rationale: Keeps the three animals, distinct losses, and the recurring no-rescuer ending.
verses.before: Your ox will be slaughtered before your eyes, but you will not eat from it. Your donkey will be robbed from before you and will not return to you. Your flock will be given to your enemies, and there will be no one to save you.
verses.after: Your ox will be slaughtered before your eyes, but you will eat none of it. Your donkey will be taken from you, and it will not return. Your flock will be handed to your enemies, with no one to rescue you.
verses.tsw_comparator: Your ox will be slaughtered before your eyes, but you will not eat from it. Your donkey will be robbed from before you and will not return to you. Your flock will be given to your enemies, and there will be no one to save you.

verses.rationale: Keeps the children’s removal and the eyes/hands images of helplessness.
verses.before: Your sons and daughters will be given to another people, and your eyes will look and fail for them all day long, but there will be no power in your hand.
verses.after: Your sons and daughters will be handed over to another people while you watch. All day your eyes will strain for them and fail, and your hands will have no power to help.
verses.tsw_comparator: Your sons and daughters will be given to another people, and your eyes will look and fail for them all day long, but there will be no power in your hand.

verses.rationale: Preserves the unknown people’s appropriation of produce and labor.
verses.before: A people whom you have not known will eat the fruit of your ground and all your labor, and you will only be oppressed and crushed all the days.
verses.after: A people you do not know will eat the fruit of your ground and all you have labored for. You will be continually oppressed and crushed.
verses.tsw_comparator: A people whom you have not known will eat the fruit of your ground and all your labor, and you will only be oppressed and crushed all the days.

verses.rationale: Keeps the link between witnessed events and madness without adding a diagnosis.
verses.before: You will become mad because of the sight that your eyes see.
verses.after: You will be driven mad by what your eyes see.
verses.tsw_comparator: You will become mad because of the sight that your eyes see.

verses.rationale: Preserves the named body parts and whole-body extent.
verses.before: The LORD will strike you on the knees and legs with severe boils from which you cannot be healed, from the sole of your foot to the crown of your head.
verses.after: The LORD will strike your knees and legs with severe boils from which you cannot be healed, from the sole of your foot to the crown of your head.
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD will strike you on the knees and legs with severe boils from which you cannot be healed, from the sole of your foot to the crown of your head.

verses.rationale: Keeps the people’s appointed king, exile, and material description of other gods.
verses.before: “The LORD will bring you and the king whom you set over you to a nation that you and your ancestors have not known, and there you will serve other gods of wood and stone.
verses.after: The LORD will lead you and the king you set over you to a nation neither you nor your ancestors have known. There you will serve other gods, gods of wood and stone.
verses.tsw_comparator: “The LORD will bring you and the king whom you set over you to a nation that you and your ancestors have not known, and there you will serve other gods of wood and stone.

verses.rationale: Retains the three forms of public disgrace and divine driving.
verses.before: You will become a horror, a proverb, and a taunt among all the peoples where the LORD leads you.
verses.after: You will become a horror, a proverb, and a taunt among all the peoples where the LORD drives you.
verses.tsw_comparator: You will become a horror, a proverb, and a taunt among all the peoples where the LORD leads you.

verses.rationale: Keeps the much/little contrast and the named crop destroyer.
verses.before: Much seed you will carry out to the field, but little you will gather, for the locust will consume it.
verses.after: You will take much seed out to the field but gather little, because locusts will consume it.
verses.tsw_comparator: Much seed you will carry out to the field, but little you will gather, for the locust will consume it.

verses.rationale: Preserves labor followed by loss of both harvest and wine.
verses.before: You will plant vineyards and cultivate them, but you will not drink wine or gather grapes, for the worm will eat them.
verses.after: You will plant and tend vineyards, but you will neither drink the wine nor gather the grapes, because worms will eat them.
verses.tsw_comparator: You will plant vineyards and cultivate them, but you will not drink wine or gather grapes, for the worm will eat them.

verses.rationale: Keeps anointing as the lost use of oil rather than replacing it with cooking.
verses.before: Olive trees you will have throughout all your territory, but you will not anoint yourself with oil, for your olives will drop off.
verses.after: You will have olive trees throughout your territory, but you will not anoint yourself with oil, because your olives will drop off.
verses.tsw_comparator: Olive trees you will have throughout all your territory, but you will not anoint yourself with oil, for your olives will drop off.

verses.rationale: Retains the painful contrast between bearing children and losing them to captivity.
verses.before: Sons and daughters you will father, but they will not be yours, for they will go into captivity.
verses.after: You will have sons and daughters, but they will not remain yours, because they will go into captivity.
verses.tsw_comparator: Sons and daughters you will father, but they will not be yours, for they will go into captivity.

verses.rationale: Uses a cautious insect designation for the uncertain chirring pest while retaining the dispossession verb.
verses.before: The cricket will possess all your trees and the fruit of your ground.
verses.after: Swarming insects will take possession of all your trees and the fruit of your ground.
verses.tsw_comparator: The cricket will possess all your trees and the fruit of your ground.

verses.rationale: Keeps the repeated upward/downward movement and the resident status.
verses.before: The resident alien who is in your midst will rise above you higher and higher, while you will descend lower and lower.
verses.after: The resident foreigner among you will rise higher and higher above you, while you sink lower and lower.
verses.tsw_comparator: The resident alien who is in your midst will rise above you higher and higher, while you will descend lower and lower.

verses.rationale: Preserves both lending and bodily reversals of the earlier blessings.
verses.before: He will lend to you, but you will not lend to him. He will be the head, and you will be the tail.
verses.after: He will lend to you, but you will not lend to him. He will be the head, and you will be the tail.
verses.tsw_comparator: He will lend to you, but you will not lend to him. He will be the head, and you will be the tail.

verses.rationale: Retains all three pursuing verbs and the stated reason.
verses.before: “All these curses will come upon you, pursue you, and overtake you until you are destroyed, because you did not listen to the voice of the LORD your God, to keep his commandments and statutes that he commanded you.
verses.after: All these curses will come upon you, pursue you, and overtake you until you are destroyed, because you did not listen to the LORD your God by keeping the commandments and statutes he gave you.
verses.tsw_comparator: “All these curses will come upon you, pursue you, and overtake you until you are destroyed, because you did not listen to the voice of the LORD your God, to keep his commandments and statutes that he commanded you.

verses.rationale: Keeps the sign/wonder terminology and enduring reach to descendants.
verses.before: They will be upon you as a sign and a wonder, and upon your offspring forever,
verses.after: They will be a sign and a wonder upon you and your descendants forever.
verses.tsw_comparator: They will be upon you as a sign and a wonder, and upon your offspring forever,

verses.rationale: Preserves the causal clause across the verse boundary and the contrast of abundance with deprivation.
verses.before: because you did not serve the LORD your God with joy and gladness of heart because of the abundance of everything.
verses.after: Because you did not serve the LORD your God with joy and a glad heart when you had an abundance of everything,
verses.tsw_comparator: because you did not serve the LORD your God with joy and gladness of heart because of the abundance of everything.

verses.rationale: Retains all four deprivations and the iron yoke, leaving the final singular agent as in the source.
verses.before: So you will serve your enemies whom the LORD will send against you, in hunger, thirst, nakedness, and lack of everything. He will put an iron yoke upon your neck until he has destroyed you.
verses.after: you will serve the enemies the LORD sends against you, in hunger, thirst, nakedness, and need of everything. He will put an iron yoke on your neck until he has destroyed you.
verses.tsw_comparator: Therefore you will serve your enemies whom the LORD will send against you, in hunger, thirst, nakedness, and lack of everything. He will put an iron yoke upon your neck until he has destroyed you.

verses.rationale: Keeps distance, bird imagery, and unfamiliar language together.
verses.before: “The LORD will raise against you a nation from far away, from the end of the earth, as an eagle swoops down, a nation whose language you do not understand,
verses.after: The LORD will bring a nation against you from far away, from the end of the earth, swooping like an eagle—a nation whose language you do not understand.
verses.tsw_comparator: “The LORD will raise against you a nation from far away, from the end of the earth, as an eagle swoops down, a nation whose language you do not understand,

verses.rationale: Preserves both age groups and their different denied responses.
verses.before: a hard-faced nation that will not respect the old or show favor to the young.
verses.after: It will be a fierce-looking nation, showing no respect for the old and no mercy to the young.
verses.tsw_comparator: a hard-faced nation that will not respect the old or show favor to the young.

verses.rationale: Retains the complete produce list and repeated destruction clauses.
verses.before: It will eat the fruit of your livestock and the fruit of your ground until you are destroyed. It will leave you no grain, new wine, or oil, no offspring of your cattle or increase of your flock, until it has caused you to perish.
verses.after: It will eat the fruit of your livestock and the fruit of your ground until you are destroyed. It will leave you no grain, new wine, oil, calves from your herds, or young from your flocks, until it has made you perish.
verses.tsw_comparator: It will eat the fruit of your livestock and the fruit of your ground until you are destroyed. It will leave you no grain, new wine, or oil, no offspring of your cattle or increase of your flock, until it has caused you to perish.

verses.rationale: Keeps the deliberately repeated siege statement and misplaced trust in walls.
verses.before: It will besiege you within all your gates until your high and fortified walls in which you trust fall throughout all your land. It will besiege you within all your gates throughout all your land that the LORD your God has given you.
verses.after: It will besiege you in all your towns until the high, fortified walls you trust come down throughout your land. It will besiege you in all your towns throughout the land the LORD your God has given you.
verses.tsw_comparator: It will besiege you within all your gates until your high and fortified walls in which you trust fall throughout all your land. It will besiege you within all your gates throughout all your land that the LORD your God has given you.

verses.rationale: Retains the fruit image and explicitly names the cannibalism rather than softening the harm.
verses.before: “You will eat the fruit of your own womb, the flesh of your sons and daughters whom the LORD your God has given you, in the siege and distress with which your enemy will distress you.
verses.after: You will eat the fruit of your womb, the flesh of the sons and daughters the LORD your God has given you, in the siege and distress your enemy brings upon you.
verses.tsw_comparator: “You will eat the fruit of your own womb, the flesh of your sons and daughters whom the LORD your God has given you, in the siege and distress with which your enemy will distress you.

verses.rationale: Keeps the relational list and the evil-eye idiom as hostility, continuing the sentence into verse 55.
verses.before: The man among you who is tender and very delicate—his eye will be evil toward his brother, toward the wife of his embrace, and toward the rest of his children whom he leaves,
verses.after: Even the gentlest, most delicate man among you will look with hostility at his brother, the wife he embraces, and the children he still has,
verses.tsw_comparator: The man among you who is tender and very delicate—his eye will be evil toward his brother, toward the wife of his embrace, and toward the rest of his children whom he leaves,

verses.rationale: Makes the withholding explicit while preserving the repeated siege cause and child victims.
verses.before: so that he does not give to any of them from the flesh of his children that he is eating, because nothing remains to him in the siege and distress with which your enemy will distress you within all your gates.
verses.after: refusing to give any of them the flesh of his children that he is eating. Nothing else will remain to him in the siege and distress your enemy brings upon you in all your towns.
verses.tsw_comparator: so that he does not give to any of them from the flesh of his children that he is eating, because nothing remains to him in the siege and distress with which your enemy will distress you within all your gates.

verses.rationale: Retains the extreme delicacy image, repetition, and all family relationships across labels.
verses.before: The tender and delicate woman among you, who would not venture to set the sole of her foot upon the ground because of delicateness and tenderness—her eye will be evil toward the husband of her embrace, toward her son and daughter,
verses.after: Even the gentlest, most delicate woman among you, who would not venture to set her foot on the ground because she was so delicate and gentle, will look with hostility at the husband she embraces, her son, and her daughter,
verses.tsw_comparator: The tender and delicate woman among you, who would not venture to set the sole of her foot upon the ground because of delicateness and tenderness—her eye will be evil toward the husband of her embrace, toward her son and daughter,

verses.rationale: Preserves afterbirth, childbirth, secrecy, and cannibalism without euphemizing the siege’s horror.
verses.before: toward her afterbirth that comes out from between her feet and toward the children whom she bears, for she will secretly eat them for lack of everything in the siege and distress with which your enemy will distress you within your gates.
verses.after: withholding the afterbirth that comes out between her legs and the children she bears. She will eat them secretly for lack of everything, in the siege and distress your enemy brings upon you in your towns.
verses.tsw_comparator: toward her afterbirth that comes out from between her feet and toward the children whom she bears, for she will secretly eat them for lack of everything in the siege and distress with which your enemy will distress you within your gates.

verses.rationale: Keeps written instruction and reverence for the named God as the condition continued in verse 59.
verses.before: “If you are not careful to do all the words of this instruction that are written in this book, to fear this glorious and fearsome name, the LORD your God,
verses.after: If you do not faithfully carry out all the words of this instruction written in this scroll, revering this glorious and fearsome name—the LORD your God—
verses.tsw_comparator: “If you are not careful to do all the words of this instruction that are written in this book, to fear this glorious and fearsome name, the LORD your God,

verses.rationale: Retains the repeated lasting quality and the reach to descendants.
verses.before: then the LORD will make extraordinary your plagues and the plagues of your offspring, great and lasting plagues, and severe and lasting sicknesses.
verses.after: the LORD will make your plagues and your descendants’ plagues extraordinary: great, lasting plagues and severe, lasting diseases.
verses.tsw_comparator: then the LORD will make extraordinary your plagues and the plagues of your offspring, great and lasting plagues, and severe and lasting sicknesses.

verses.rationale: Keeps return of Egyptian disease and the recurring cling image.
verses.before: He will bring back upon you all the diseases of Egypt that you feared, and they will cling to you.
verses.after: He will bring back upon you all the diseases of Egypt that you dreaded, and they will cling to you.
verses.tsw_comparator: He will bring back upon you all the diseases of Egypt that you feared, and they will cling to you.

verses.rationale: Preserves the extension beyond the written list without adding examples.
verses.before: Also every sickness and every plague that is not written in the book of this instruction, the LORD will bring upon you until you are destroyed.
verses.after: The LORD will also bring upon you every disease and plague not written in this scroll of instruction, until you are destroyed.
verses.tsw_comparator: Also every sickness and every plague that is not written in the book of this instruction, the LORD will bring upon you until you are destroyed.

verses.rationale: Keeps the reversal of the ancestral star promise and its explicit cause.
verses.before: You will be left few in number, though you were as numerous as the stars of the heavens, because you did not listen to the voice of the LORD your God.
verses.after: You will be left few in number, though you were as numerous as the stars of the heavens, because you did not listen to the LORD your God.
verses.tsw_comparator: You will be left few in number, though you were as numerous as the stars of the heavens, because you did not listen to the voice of the LORD your God.

verses.rationale: Preserves the unsettling repeated divine rejoicing and the uprooting rather than explaining them away.
verses.before: And it will be, just as the LORD rejoiced over you to do you good and multiply you, so the LORD will cause you to perish and destroy you, and you will be torn from the ground that you are entering to possess.
verses.after: Just as the LORD rejoiced over you in doing you good and multiplying you, so the LORD will rejoice over you in making you perish and destroying you. You will be torn from the ground you are entering to possess.
verses.tsw_comparator: And it will be, just as the LORD rejoiced over you to do you good and multiply you, so the LORD will cause you to perish and destroy you, and you will be torn from the ground that you are entering to possess.

verses.rationale: Keeps worldwide dispersal and the repeated unknown wood-and-stone gods.
verses.before: “The LORD will scatter you among all the peoples, from one end of the earth to the other end of the earth. There you will serve other gods whom you and your ancestors have not known, wood and stone.
verses.after: The LORD will scatter you among all peoples, from one end of the earth to the other. There you will serve other gods neither you nor your ancestors have known, gods of wood and stone.
verses.tsw_comparator: “The LORD will scatter you among all the peoples, from one end of the earth to the other end of the earth. There you will serve other gods whom you and your ancestors have not known, wood and stone.

verses.rationale: Retains rest/foot imagery and the three bodily or inward effects.
verses.before: Among those nations you will find no rest, and there will be no resting place for the sole of your foot. The LORD will give you there a trembling heart, failing eyes, and despairing life.
verses.after: Among those nations you will find no rest, no resting place for the sole of your foot. There the LORD will give you a trembling heart, failing eyes, and a languishing soul.
verses.tsw_comparator: Among those nations you will find no rest, and there will be no resting place for the sole of your foot. The LORD will give you there a trembling heart, failing eyes, and despairing life.

verses.rationale: Keeps life hanging and repeats life at the close of the verse.
verses.before: Your life will hang in suspense before you. You will fear night and day and will have no assurance of your life.
verses.after: Your life will hang in doubt before you. Night and day you will be afraid, with no assurance of your life.
verses.tsw_comparator: Your life will hang in suspense before you. You will fear night and day and will have no assurance of your life.

verses.rationale: Preserves the reciprocal morning/evening cries and heart/eyes causes.
verses.before: In the morning you will say, ‘If only it were evening!’ and in the evening you will say, ‘If only it were morning!’ because of the fear that your heart fears and because of the sight that your eyes see.
verses.after: In the morning you will say, ‘If only it were evening!’ And in the evening you will say, ‘If only it were morning!’ Such will be the dread in your heart and the sights before your eyes.
verses.tsw_comparator: In the morning you will say, ‘If only it were evening!’ and in the evening you will say, ‘If only it were morning!’ because of the fear that your heart fears and because of the sight that your eyes see.

verses.rationale: Keeps ships, the reversed return prohibition, both slave sexes, and unsuccessful self-sale.
verses.before: The LORD will bring you back to Egypt in ships, by a way of which I said to you, ‘You will never see it again.’ There you will offer yourselves for sale to your enemies as male and female servants, but there will be no buyer.”
verses.after: The LORD will take you back to Egypt in ships, along the route I told you that you would never see again. There you will offer yourselves for sale to your enemies as male and female slaves, but there will be no buyer.”
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD will bring you back to Egypt in ships, by a way of which I said to you, ‘You shall never see it again.’ There you will offer yourselves for sale to your enemies as male and female servants, but there will be no buyer.”

verses.rationale: Binds public 29:1 to Hebrew 28:69 and preserves the covenant’s relationship to Horeb.
verses.before: These are the words of the covenant that the LORD commanded Moses to make with the children of Israel in the land of Moab, besides the covenant that he made with them at Horeb.
verses.after: These are the words of the covenant the LORD commanded Moses to make with the Israelites in the land of Moab, in addition to the covenant he made with them at Horeb.
verses.tsw_comparator: These are the words of the covenant that the LORD commanded Moses to make with the children of Israel in the land of Moab, besides the covenant that he made with them at Horeb.

verses.rationale: Preserves the eyewitness address and all three recipients of the Egyptian acts.
verses.before: Moses called to all Israel and said to them: “You yourselves have seen all that the LORD did before your eyes in the land of Egypt to Pharaoh, to all his servants, and to all his land—
verses.after: Moses called all Israel together and said to them, “You yourselves have seen everything the LORD did before your eyes in Egypt to Pharaoh, to all his servants, and to all his land.
verses.tsw_comparator: Moses called to all Israel and said to them: “You yourselves have seen all that the LORD did before your eyes in the land of Egypt to Pharaoh, to all his servants, and to all his land—

verses.rationale: Retains the three event descriptions and renewed emphasis on seeing.
verses.before: the great trials that your eyes saw, the signs, and those great wonders.
verses.after: Your eyes saw the great trials, those great signs and wonders.
verses.tsw_comparator: the great trials that your eyes saw, the signs, and those great wonders.

verses.rationale: Keeps divine non-giving as stated rather than substituting a claim that the people simply refused.
verses.before: Yet the LORD has not given you a heart to know, eyes to see, or ears to hear, to this day.
verses.after: Yet to this day the LORD has not given you a heart to understand, eyes to see, or ears to hear.
verses.tsw_comparator: Yet the LORD has not given you a heart to know, eyes to see, or ears to hear, to this day.

verses.rationale: Preserves the first-person divine voice within Moses’ speech, forty years, and repeated non-wearing.
verses.before: I led you forty years in the wilderness. Your garments did not wear out upon you, and your sandal did not wear out upon your foot.
verses.after: I led you through the wilderness for forty years. The clothes on you did not wear out, and the sandals on your feet did not wear out.
verses.tsw_comparator: I led you forty years in the wilderness. Your garments did not wear out upon you, and your sandal did not wear out upon your foot.

verses.rationale: Retains the explicit divine self-identification and the three absent foods or drinks.
verses.before: You did not eat bread and did not drink wine or strong drink, so that you might know that I am the LORD your God.
verses.after: You ate no bread and drank no wine or strong drink, so that you would know that I am the LORD your God.
verses.tsw_comparator: You did not eat bread and did not drink wine or strong drink, so that you might know that I am the LORD your God.

verses.rationale: Keeps the shift from you to us/we and correctly pairs both kings and territories.
verses.before: When you came to this place, Sihon king of Heshbon and Og king of Bashan came out to meet us for battle, and we struck them.
verses.after: When you came to this place, Sihon king of Heshbon and Og king of Bashan came out to fight us, and we defeated them.
verses.tsw_comparator: When you came to this place, Sihon king of Heshbon and Og king of Bashan came out to meet us for battle, and we struck them.

verses.rationale: Preserves the half-tribe qualification and the three recipients.
verses.before: We took their land and gave it as an inheritance to the Reubenites, the Gadites, and the half-tribe of Manasseh.
verses.after: We took their land and gave it as an inheritance to the Reubenites, the Gadites, and half the tribe of Manasseh.
verses.tsw_comparator: We took their land and gave it as an inheritance to the Reubenites, the Gadites, and the half-tribe of Manasseh.

verses.rationale: Links keeping and doing to the success or wise conduct sense of the final verb.
verses.before: So keep the words of this covenant and do them, so that you may act wisely in all that you do.
verses.after: So keep the words of this covenant and carry them out, so that you may succeed in everything you do.
verses.tsw_comparator: So keep the words of this covenant and do them, so that you may act wisely in all that you do.

verses.rationale: Retains the source’s separate heads and tribes wording and continues its participant list.
verses.before: “You are standing today, all of you, before the LORD your God: your heads, your tribes, your elders, your officers, every man of Israel,
verses.after: All of you stand today before the LORD your God: your heads, your tribes, your elders and officers, all the men of Israel,
verses.tsw_comparator: “You are standing today, all of you, before the LORD your God: your heads, your tribes, your elders, your officers, every man of Israel,

verses.rationale: Keeps women, children, resident foreigners, and the two labor roles within the assembly.
verses.before: your little children, your wives, and the resident alien who is among your camp, from the one who cuts your wood to the one who draws your water,
verses.after: your children, your wives, and the resident foreigner within your camp, from the one who cuts your wood to the one who draws your water.
verses.tsw_comparator: your little children, your wives, and the resident alien who is in the midst of your camp, from the one who cuts your wood to the one who draws your water,

verses.rationale: Makes the sanction-bearing force of the oath explicit while continuing its purpose into verse 13.
verses.before: so that you may enter into the covenant of the LORD your God and into his oath that the LORD your God is making with you today,
verses.after: You are here to enter the covenant of the LORD your God, with its binding oath and curse, which the LORD your God is making with you today,
verses.tsw_comparator: so that you may enter into the covenant of the LORD your God and into his oath that the LORD your God is making with you today,

verses.rationale: Preserves both sides of the covenant relationship and all three named ancestors.
verses.before: in order to establish you today as his people and that he may be your God, as he spoke to you and as he swore to your ancestors, to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.
verses.after: so that he may establish you today as his people and be your God, as he promised you and swore to your ancestors Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.
verses.tsw_comparator: in order to establish you today as his people and that he may be your God, as he spoke to you and as he swore to your ancestors, to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.

verses.rationale: Retains the oath terminology and the incomplete contrast across labels.
verses.before: And not with you alone am I making this covenant and this oath,
verses.after: I am making this covenant, with its oath and curse, not with you alone,
verses.tsw_comparator: And not with you alone am I making this covenant and this oath,

verses.rationale: Keeps the present and absent parties without limiting the absent to a single explanation.
verses.before: but with whoever is standing here with us today before the LORD our God and with whoever is not here with us today.
verses.after: but both with those standing here with us today before the LORD our God and with those who are not here with us today.
verses.tsw_comparator: but with whoever is standing here with us today before the LORD our God and with whoever is not here with us today.

verses.rationale: Preserves the shared memory and the two stages of the journey.
verses.before: “For you yourselves know how we lived in the land of Egypt and how we passed through the midst of the nations through which you passed.
verses.after: You know how we lived in Egypt and how we passed through the nations along the way.
verses.tsw_comparator: “For you yourselves know how we lived in the land of Egypt and how we passed through the midst of the nations through which you passed.

verses.rationale: Retains the contemptuous idol terminology and all four materials.
verses.before: You saw their detestable things and their idols of wood and stone, silver and gold, that were among them.
verses.after: You saw their detestable things and their filthy idols of wood and stone, silver and gold, there among them.
verses.tsw_comparator: You saw their detestable things and their idols of wood and stone, silver and gold, that were among them.

verses.rationale: Keeps the four social units, inward turning, and the poisonous-root image.
verses.before: Lest there be among you a man or woman, clan or tribe, whose heart turns away today from the LORD our God to go and serve the gods of those nations; lest there be among you a root bearing poisonous and bitter fruit;
verses.after: Make sure there is no man or woman, clan or tribe among you whose heart turns away today from the LORD our God to go and serve the gods of those nations. Make sure no root among you produces poison and wormwood.
verses.tsw_comparator: Lest there be among you a man or woman, clan or tribe, whose heart turns away today from the LORD our God to go and serve the gods of those nations; lest there be among you a root bearing poisonous and bitter fruit;

verses.rationale: Retains divine heart-circumcision and its love-and-life purpose rather than replacing the biblical image.

verses.rationale: Keeps the conditional force, written instruction, and final heart/soul return.

verses.rationale: Keeps the ascent, retrieval, hearing, and doing sequence in the rhetorical question.

verses.after: Nor is it beyond the sea, so that you must ask, ‘Who will cross the sea for us and bring it to us, so that we can hear it and carry it out?’

verses.rationale: Keeps the inward turning and two acts of religious allegiance in the conditional clause.

verses.rationale: Preserves the cosmic witnesses and links choosing life to both generations across labels.
