verses.before: “And now write for yourselves this song and teach it to the children of Israel. Put it in their mouths, so that this song may be for me as a witness against the children of Israel.
verses.after: Now write down this song, both of you. Moses, teach it to the Israelites and put it in their mouths, so that this song may be my witness against the Israelites.
verses.tsw_comparator: “And now write for yourselves this song and teach it to the children of Israel. Put it in their mouths, so that this song may be for me as a witness against the children of Israel.

verses.rationale: Preserves abundance, fatness, and the sequence of covenant betrayal.
verses.before: For when I bring them into the ground that I swore to their ancestors, flowing with milk and honey, and they eat and are satisfied and grow fat, they will turn to other gods and serve them and despise me and break my covenant.
verses.after: When I bring them into the land flowing with milk and honey that I swore to their ancestors, they will eat their fill and grow fat. Then they will turn to other gods and serve them, spurn me, and break my covenant.
verses.tsw_comparator: For when I bring them into the ground that I swore to their ancestors, flowing with milk and honey, and they eat and are satisfied and grow fat, they will turn to other gods and serve them and despise me and break my covenant.

verses.rationale: Retains the song’s answering and mouth imagery and God’s knowledge before entry.
verses.before: Then, when many evils and distresses find them, this song will answer before them as a witness, for it will not be forgotten from the mouth of their offspring. For I know the inclination that they are forming today, before I bring them into the land that I swore to give them.”
verses.after: When many calamities and troubles find them, this song will answer as a witness against them, because it will not be forgotten from the mouths of their descendants. I know what they are inclined to do even now, before I bring them into the land I swore to give them.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Then, when many evils and distresses find them, this song will answer before them as a witness, for it will not be forgotten from the mouth of their offspring. For I know the inclination that they are forming today, before I bring them into the land that I swore to give them.”

verses.rationale: Keeps same-day writing and teaching as the fulfillment of the instruction.
verses.before: So Moses wrote this song on that day and taught it to the children of Israel.
verses.after: Moses wrote down this song that day and taught it to the Israelites.
verses.tsw_comparator: So Moses wrote this song on that day and taught it to the children of Israel.

verses.rationale: Identifies the implicit divine commissioner from the first-person oath and keeps bring distinct from verse 7.
verses.before: The LORD commanded Joshua son of Nun and said, “Be strong and courageous, for you will bring the children of Israel into the land that I swore to them, and I will be with you.”
verses.after: The LORD commissioned Joshua son of Nun: “Be strong and courageous, for you will bring the Israelites into the land I swore to give them, and I will be with you.”
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD commanded Joshua son of Nun and said, “Be strong and courageous, for you shall bring the children of Israel into the land that I swore to them, and I will be with you.”

verses.rationale: Preserves completion of the writing while continuing the sentence into the command.
verses.before: When Moses had finished writing the words of this instruction in a book until they were complete,
verses.after: When Moses had finished writing all the words of this instruction in a scroll,
verses.tsw_comparator: When Moses had finished writing the words of this instruction in a book until they were complete,

verses.rationale: Keeps the carriers as recipients of the ensuing storage command.
verses.before: Moses commanded the Levites who carried the ark of the covenant of the LORD, saying,
verses.after: he commanded the Levites who carried the ark of the LORD’s covenant:
verses.tsw_comparator: Moses commanded the Levites who carried the ark of the covenant of the LORD, saying,

verses.rationale: Preserves beside rather than inside the ark and the scroll’s witness function.
verses.before: “Take this book of instruction and put it beside the ark of the covenant of the LORD your God, and it will be there as a witness against you.
verses.after: “Take this scroll of instruction and place it beside the ark of the covenant of the LORD your God. It is to remain there as a witness against you.
verses.tsw_comparator: “Take this book of instruction and put it beside the ark of the covenant of the LORD your God, and it shall be there as a witness against you.

verses.rationale: Keeps stiff-neck imagery and the argument from present rebellion to future rebellion.
verses.before: For I know your rebellion and your stiff neck. Look, while I am still alive with you today, you have been rebellious against the LORD; how much more after my death!
verses.after: I know your rebellion and your stiff neck. Even now, while I am still alive among you, you have rebelled against the LORD. How much more after my death!
verses.tsw_comparator: For I know your rebellion and your stiff neck. Look, while I am still alive with you today, you have been rebellious against the LORD; how much more after my death!

verses.rationale: Retains the specified leaders and the returning cosmic witnesses.
verses.before: Gather to me all the elders of your tribes and your officers, and I will speak these words in their hearing and call the heavens and the earth as witnesses against them.
verses.after: Gather to me all the elders of your tribes and your officers. I will speak these words in their hearing and call the heavens and the earth as witnesses against them.
verses.tsw_comparator: Gather to me all the elders of your tribes and your officers, and I will speak these words in their hearing and call the heavens and the earth as witnesses against them.

verses.rationale: Keeps emphatic corruption, path departure, future calamity, and hand-made provocation.
verses.before: For I know that after my death you will surely act corruptly and turn aside from the way that I commanded you. Evil will meet you in the latter days because you will do what is evil in the eyes of the LORD, provoking him to anger through the work of your hands.”
verses.after: I know that after my death you will act utterly corruptly and turn away from the path I commanded you. In days to come calamity will meet you, because you will do what is evil in the LORD’s sight, provoking him with the work of your hands.”
verses.tsw_comparator: For I know that after my death you will surely act corruptly and turn aside from the way that I commanded you. Evil will meet you in the latter days because you will do what is evil in the eyes of the LORD, provoking him to anger through the work of your hands.”

verses.rationale: Preserves complete recitation and the full assembly audience before the song begins.
verses.before: Then Moses spoke in the hearing of all the assembly of Israel the words of this song until they were completed:
verses.after: Then Moses spoke all the words of this song, from beginning to end, in the hearing of the whole assembly of Israel.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then Moses spoke in the hearing of all the assembly of Israel the words of this song until they were completed:

verses.rationale: Keeps the two cosmic audiences in parallel poetic lines without adding quotation marks around the whole song.
verses.before: Give ear, O heavens, and I will speak; let the earth hear the words of my mouth.
verses.after: Listen, heavens, and I will speak. Let the earth hear the words of my mouth.
verses.tsw_comparator: Give ear, O heavens, and I will speak; let the earth hear the words of my mouth.

verses.rationale: Preserves four moisture-and-growth comparisons rather than reducing them to one image.
verses.before: May my teaching drop like rain, my word distill like dew, like showers upon young grass and like abundant rain upon plants.
verses.after: May my teaching fall like rain, my speech settle like dew, like showers on tender grass, like rain on growing plants.
verses.tsw_comparator: May my teaching drop like rain, my word distill like dew, like showers upon young grass and like abundant rain upon plants.

verses.rationale: Keeps proclamation followed by the plural summons to acknowledge divine greatness.
verses.before: For I will proclaim the name of the LORD. Give greatness to our God!
verses.after: For I will proclaim the LORD’s name. Give greatness to our God!
verses.tsw_comparator: For I will proclaim the name of the LORD. Give greatness to our God!

verses.rationale: Retains Rock as the song’s repeated divine title and all four justice/faithfulness descriptions.
verses.before: The Rock—his work is perfect, for all his ways are justice. A God of faithfulness and without injustice, righteous and upright is he.
verses.after: The Rock—his work is complete, for all his ways are justice. A faithful God, with no injustice, righteous and upright is he.
verses.tsw_comparator: The Rock—his work is perfect, for all his ways are justice. A God of faithfulness and without injustice, righteous and upright is he.

verses.rationale: Preserves the elliptical not-his-children and blemish clauses without adding an unsupported temporal no longer.
verses.before: They have acted corruptly toward him; they are not his children—their blemish. They are a twisted and crooked generation.
verses.after: They have acted corruptly toward him; not his children—the blemish is theirs! A crooked and twisted generation.
verses.tsw_comparator: They have acted corruptly toward him; they are not his children—their blemish. They are a twisted and crooked generation.

verses.rationale: Uses created for the acquire/create verb while retaining fatherhood and the other two making verbs.
verses.before: Is this how you repay the LORD, foolish and unwise people? Is he not your father who acquired you? He made you and established you.
verses.after: Is this how you repay the LORD, foolish and unwise people? Is he not your father who created you, who made you and established you?
verses.tsw_comparator: Is this how you repay the LORD, foolish and unwise people? Is he not your father who acquired you? He made you and established you.

verses.rationale: Keeps the multigenerational memory and the distinct father/elders sources of testimony.
verses.before: Remember the days of old; consider the years of generation after generation. Ask your father, and he will tell you; your elders, and they will say to you.
verses.after: Remember the days of old; consider the years of generation after generation. Ask your father, and he will tell you, your elders, and they will speak to you.
verses.tsw_comparator: Remember the days of old; consider the years of generation after generation. Ask your father, and he will tell you; your elders, and they will say to you.

verses.rationale: Follows pinned children of Israel rather than importing sons of God; retains Adam and inheritance imagery.
verses.before: When the Most High gave the nations their inheritance, when he divided the children of humanity, he set the boundaries of the peoples according to the number of the sons of God.
verses.after: When the Most High gave nations their inheritance, when he divided the children of Adam, he set the boundaries of peoples according to the number of the children of Israel.
verses.tsw_comparator: When the Most High gave the nations their inheritance, when he divided the children of humanity, he set the boundaries of the peoples according to the number of the sons of God.

verses.rationale: Keeps the compact parallel identifying Jacob as the divine allotment.
verses.before: For the LORD’s portion is his people; Jacob is the measured share of his inheritance.
verses.after: For the LORD’s portion is his people, Jacob his allotted inheritance.
verses.tsw_comparator: For the LORD’s portion is his people; Jacob is the measured share of his inheritance.

verses.rationale: Retains collective Jacob as him and the protective pupil image within the desert setting.
verses.before: He found him in a wilderness land, in a waste, a howling emptiness. He surrounded him; he cared for him; he guarded him as the pupil of his eye.
verses.after: He found him in a wilderness land, in an empty, howling waste. He surrounded him, cared for him, and guarded him like the pupil of his eye.
verses.tsw_comparator: He found him in a wilderness land, in a waste, a howling emptiness. He surrounded him; he cared for him; he guarded him as the pupil of his eye.

verses.rationale: Preserves the eagle comparison and singular protected people without converting it into explanatory prose.
verses.before: Like an eagle that stirs up its nest, that hovers over its young, he spread his wings, took him, and carried him upon his pinions.
verses.after: Like an eagle stirring its nest, hovering over its young, he spread his wings and took him up; he carried him on his pinions.
verses.tsw_comparator: Like an eagle that stirs up its nest, that hovers over its young, he spread his wings, took him, and carried him upon his pinions.

verses.rationale: Keeps exclusive guidance and the separate denial of a foreign companion deity.
verses.before: The LORD alone guided him, and no foreign god was with him.
verses.after: The LORD alone guided him; no foreign god was with him.
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD alone guided him, and no foreign god was with him.

verses.rationale: Follows the recorded read form for heights and preserves the striking suckling-from-rock images. Consistency refinement: Separates the Hebrew causative made-him-ride from the following finite he-ate clause. Naming the LORD and Jacob, already identified in 32:9–12, makes the two agents audible while preserving the rock/honey/oil images and poetic lineation.
verses.before: He made him ride upon the heights of the land, and he ate the produce of the field. He made him suck honey from the rock and oil from the flinty rock,
verses.after: The LORD made Jacob ride the heights of the earth, and Jacob ate the produce of the fields. The LORD let him suck honey from rock and oil from flinty stone.
verses.tsw_comparator: He made him ride upon the heights of the land, and he ate the produce of the field. He made him suck honey from the rock and oil from the flinty rock,

consistency_history.prior_after: He made him ride the heights of the earth and eat the produce of the fields. He let him suck honey from rock and oil from flinty stone.
consistency_history.prior_rationale: Follows the recorded read form for heights and preserves the striking suckling-from-rock images.
consistency_history.rationale: Separates the Hebrew causative made-him-ride from the following finite he-ate clause. Naming the LORD and Jacob, already identified in 32:9–12, makes the two agents audible while preserving the rock/honey/oil images and poetic lineation.

verses.rationale: Keeps the complete food list, shifts to you, and blood-of-grapes image; renders wheat-kidney fat idiom in the text and explains it in a note.
verses.before: curds from cattle and milk from the flock, with fat of lambs, rams of Bashan, and goats, with the finest wheat; and from the blood of grapes you drank wine.
verses.after: Curds from cattle and milk from flocks, with fat lambs, rams from Bashan and goats, with the richest kernels of wheat— and you drank wine, the blood of grapes.
verses.tsw_comparator: curds from cattle and milk from the flock, with fat of lambs, rams of Bashan, and goats, with the finest wheat; and from the blood of grapes you drank wine.

verses.rationale: Retains Jeshurun, the abrupt you/he movement, and the contrast between nourishment and abandonment.
verses.before: Yet Jeshurun grew fat and kicked. You grew fat, thick, and sleek. Then he abandoned the God who made him and treated with contempt the Rock of his salvation.
verses.after: Jeshurun grew fat and kicked— you grew fat, thick, and gorged! He abandoned the God who made him and treated the Rock of his salvation with contempt.
verses.tsw_comparator: But Jeshurun grew fat and kicked. You grew fat, thick, and sleek. Then he abandoned the God who made him and treated with contempt the Rock of his salvation.

verses.rationale: Keeps jealousy and anger paired and supplies gods from the immediate context for foreign things.
verses.before: They made him jealous with foreign gods; with detestable things they provoked him to anger.
verses.after: They made him jealous with foreign gods; with detestable things they provoked him to anger.
verses.tsw_comparator: They made him jealous with foreign gods; with detestable things they provoked him to anger.

verses.rationale: Preserves demons, recent novelty, and the shift to your ancestors.
verses.before: They sacrificed to demons, not God, to gods they had not known, new ones that came recently, whom your ancestors did not dread.
verses.after: They sacrificed to demons, not God, to gods they had not known, new ones that had lately come, whom your ancestors did not dread.
verses.tsw_comparator: They sacrificed to demons, not God, to gods they had not known, new ones that came recently, whom your ancestors did not dread.

verses.rationale: Retains both fathering and birth-labor imagery for God instead of harmonizing them to a single parental image.
verses.before: You neglected the Rock who fathered you, and forgot the God who gave you birth.
verses.after: You neglected the Rock who fathered you and forgot the God who gave you birth.
verses.tsw_comparator: You neglected the Rock who fathered you, and forgot the God who gave you birth.

verses.rationale: Keeps the explicit inclusion of daughters alongside sons and divine rejection.
verses.before: The LORD saw and rejected them because of the provocation of his sons and daughters.
verses.after: The LORD saw and rejected them, provoked by his sons and daughters.
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD saw and rejected them because of the provocation of his sons and daughters.

verses.rationale: Marks the divine speech and retains face-hiding, final outcome, and faithlessness.
verses.before: He said: “I will hide my face from them; I will see what their end will be. For they are a generation of reversals, children in whom there is no faithfulness.
verses.after: He said, “I will hide my face from them and see what their end will be. For they are a perverse generation, children with no faithfulness in them.
verses.tsw_comparator: He said: “I will hide my face from them; I will see what their end will be. For they are a generation of reversals, children in whom there is no faithfulness.

verses.rationale: Preserves the no-god/no-people and jealousy/anger reversals without importing a later identity for the nation.
verses.before: They made me jealous with what is not God; they provoked me with their empty things. So I will make them jealous with people who are not a people; with a foolish nation I will provoke them.
verses.after: They made me jealous with what is no god; they angered me with their empty things. So I will make them jealous with what is no people; with a foolish nation I will anger them.
verses.tsw_comparator: They made me jealous with what is not God; they provoked me with their empty things. So I will make them jealous with those who are not a people; with a foolish nation I will provoke them.

verses.rationale: Retains Sheol and the cosmic reach through earth, produce, and mountain foundations.
verses.before: For a fire is kindled in my anger and burns as far as deepest Sheol. It devours the earth and its produce and sets ablaze the foundations of the mountains.
verses.after: A fire has been kindled in my anger; it burns to the depths of Sheol. It consumes the earth and its produce and sets the mountains’ foundations ablaze.
verses.tsw_comparator: For a fire is kindled in my anger and burns as far as deepest Sheol. It devours the earth and its produce and sets ablaze the foundations of the mountains.

verses.rationale: Keeps calamity and exhausted arrows as parallel divine threats.
verses.before: I will heap disasters upon them; I will spend my arrows against them.
verses.after: I will heap calamities upon them and spend all my arrows on them.
verses.tsw_comparator: I will heap disasters upon them; I will spend my arrows against them.

verses.rationale: Preserves hunger, two disease forces, wild teeth, and crawling venom while avoiding certainty about obscure disease names.
verses.before: Wasted by hunger, consumed by fever and bitter plague, I will send against them the teeth of beasts, with the venom of creatures crawling in dust.
verses.after: Wasted by hunger, consumed by burning plague and bitter pestilence, they will face the teeth of beasts I send, and the venom of creatures that crawl in the dust.
verses.tsw_comparator: Wasted by hunger, consumed by fever and bitter plague, I will send against them the teeth of beasts, with the venom of creatures crawling in dust.

verses.rationale: Keeps external/internal threats and all four groups: young man, virgin, nursing infant, and gray-haired man.
verses.before: Outside, the sword will bereave; inside, terror— young man and young woman alike, nursing child and gray-haired man.
verses.after: Outside, the sword will bereave; inside their rooms, terror— for young man and virgin alike, for nursing infant and gray-haired man.
verses.tsw_comparator: Outside, the sword will bereave; inside, terror— young man and young woman alike, nursing child and gray-haired man.

verses.rationale: Selects scatter for the rare disputed verb and retains the stated intent to erase human remembrance.
verses.before: I said, ‘I will scatter them; I will make their memory cease from humanity,’
verses.after: I said, ‘I would scatter them, wipe out their memory from humankind,’
verses.tsw_comparator: I said, ‘I will scatter them; I will make their memory cease from humanity,’

verses.rationale: Keeps the difficult divine feared language and the enemies’ denial of divine agency, then closes this speech.
verses.before: if I had not feared the provocation of the enemy, lest their adversaries misunderstand and say, ‘Our hand is exalted; the LORD did not do all this.’
verses.after: but I feared the enemy’s provocation, lest their foes misunderstand and say, ‘Our own hand is triumphant; the LORD did none of this.’”
verses.tsw_comparator: if I had not feared the provocation of the enemy, lest their adversaries misunderstand and say, ‘Our hand is exalted; the LORD did not do all this.’

verses.rationale: Leaves they unidentified because the song’s movement between Israel and enemies is consequentially ambiguous.
verses.before: For they are a nation without counsel, and there is no understanding in them.
verses.after: For they are a nation empty of counsel, with no understanding among them.
verses.tsw_comparator: For they are a nation without counsel, and there is no understanding in them.

verses.rationale: Preserves the wished-for wisdom and attention to final outcome.
verses.before: If only they were wise, they would understand this; they would discern their latter end.
verses.after: If only they were wise, they would understand this; they would discern their end.
verses.tsw_comparator: If only they were wise, they would understand this; they would discern their latter end.

verses.rationale: Keeps the exact numerical pairs and the divine selling and handing-over images.
verses.before: How could one chase a thousand, and two put ten thousand to flight, unless their Rock had sold them and the LORD had handed them over?
verses.after: How could one pursue a thousand, and two put ten thousand to flight, unless their Rock had sold them and the LORD had handed them over?
verses.tsw_comparator: How could one chase a thousand, and two put ten thousand to flight, unless their Rock had sold them and the LORD had handed them over?

verses.rationale: Retains the our/their distinction and the compressed enemies-as-judges phrase rather than resolving every referent.
verses.before: For their rock is not like our Rock, even our enemies being judges.
verses.after: For their rock is not like our Rock, even our enemies being judges.
verses.tsw_comparator: For their rock is not like our Rock, even our enemies being judges.

verses.rationale: Keeps both place names, vine origin, and repeated grape language without allegorizing the fruit.
verses.before: For their vine is from the vine of Sodom and from the fields of Gomorrah. Their grapes are grapes of poison; their clusters are bitter.
verses.after: Their vine comes from Sodom’s vine and from the fields of Gomorrah. Their grapes are poisonous grapes, their clusters bitter.
verses.tsw_comparator: For their vine is from the vine of Sodom and from the fields of Gomorrah. Their grapes are grapes of poison; their clusters are bitter.

verses.rationale: Preserves the paired serpent-poison images and the wine metaphor.
verses.before: Their wine is the venom of serpents and the cruel poison of cobras.
verses.after: Their wine is the venom of serpents, the cruel poison of cobras.
verses.tsw_comparator: Their wine is the venom of serpents and the cruel poison of cobras.

verses.rationale: Marks renewed divine first-person speech without adding an otherwise absent reporting clause.
verses.before: Is this not stored up with me, sealed in my treasuries?
verses.after: “Is this not stored up with me, sealed in my storehouses?
verses.tsw_comparator: Is this not stored up with me, sealed in my treasuries?

verses.rationale: Preserves divine possession of vengeance, the slipping foot, and approaching disaster.
verses.before: Vengeance belongs to me, and repayment, for the time when their foot slips. For the day of their disaster is near, and what is prepared for them hurries toward them.
verses.after: Vengeance and repayment are mine, for the time when their foot slips. Their day of disaster is near; what awaits them comes quickly.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Vengeance belongs to me, and repayment, for the time when their foot slips. For the day of their disaster is near, and what is prepared for them hurries toward them.

verses.rationale: Chooses vindicate and compassion in context while retaining the uncertain confined/free totality formula.
verses.before: For the LORD will judge his people and have compassion on his servants when he sees that strength is gone and there is none left, slave or free.
verses.after: For the LORD will vindicate his people and have compassion on his servants, when he sees their power is gone and no one remains, confined or free.
verses.tsw_comparator: For the LORD will judge his people and have compassion on his servants when he sees that strength is gone and there is none left, slave or free.

verses.rationale: Keeps the divine taunt and refuge-rock image across the verse boundary.
verses.before: Then he will say: “Where are their gods, the rock in which they took refuge,
verses.after: He will say, “Where are their gods, the rock in which they took refuge,
verses.tsw_comparator: Then he will say: “Where are their gods, the rock in which they took refuge,

verses.rationale: Preserves both sacrificial foods and the challenged gods’ inability to provide aid and covering.
verses.before: who ate the fat of their sacrifices and drank the wine of their drink offerings? Let them rise and help you! Let them be a shelter over you!
verses.after: the gods who ate the fat of their sacrifices and drank the wine of their drink offerings? Let them rise up and help you; let them be a shelter over you!
verses.tsw_comparator: who ate the fat of their sacrifices and drank the wine of their drink offerings? Let them rise and help you! Let them be a shelter over you!

verses.rationale: Retains emphatic repeated I and both opposed pairs under a single divine agent.
verses.before: See now that I, I am he, and there is no god beside me. I put to death, and I make alive. I wound, and I heal, and there is no one who rescues from my hand.
verses.after: See now: I, I am he; there is no god beside me. I put to death and bring to life; I wound and I heal. No one can rescue from my hand.
verses.tsw_comparator: See now that I, I am he, and there is no god beside me. I put to death, and I make alive. I wound, and I heal, and there is no one who rescues from my hand.

verses.rationale: Preserves the raised-hand oath and opens the nested oath continuing through verse 42.
verses.before: For I lift my hand to the heavens and say, ‘As I live forever,
verses.after: I lift my hand to the heavens and declare, ‘As I live forever,
verses.tsw_comparator: For I lift my hand to the heavens and say, ‘As I live forever,

verses.rationale: Keeps sword, hand, judgment, and doubled repayment rather than abstracting away the martial images.
verses.before: when I sharpen my flashing sword and my hand takes hold of judgment, I will return vengeance upon my adversaries and repay people who hate me.
verses.after: when I sharpen my flashing sword and my hand takes hold of judgment, I will repay my enemies with vengeance and repay those who hate me.
verses.tsw_comparator: when I sharpen my flashing sword and my hand takes hold of judgment, I will return vengeance upon my adversaries and repay those who hate me.

verses.rationale: Retains personified weapons, captive victims, and the difficult long-haired-head reading with alternatives noted.
verses.before: I will make my arrows drunk with blood, and my sword will devour flesh— with the blood of the slain and captives, from the long-haired heads of the enemy.’
verses.after: I will make my arrows drunk with blood, and my sword will eat flesh— blood of the slain and the captives, from the long-haired heads of the enemy.’”
verses.tsw_comparator: I will make my arrows drunk with blood, and my sword will devour flesh— with the blood of the slain and captives, from the long-haired heads of the enemy.’

verses.rationale: Follows the shorter pinned stanza; supplies with for the compact opening and preserves land/people in the atonement close.
verses.before: Rejoice, O nations, with his people, for he will avenge the blood of his servants. He will return vengeance upon his adversaries and make atonement for his land and his people.
verses.after: Rejoice, nations, with his people! For he will avenge the blood of his servants, take vengeance on his enemies, and make atonement for his land and his people.
verses.tsw_comparator: Rejoice, O nations, with his people, for he will avenge the blood of his servants. He will return vengeance upon his adversaries and make atonement for his land and his people.

verses.rationale: Keeps the pinned name Hoshea rather than silently harmonizing it to Joshua.
verses.before: Moses came and spoke all the words of this song in the hearing of the people, he and Joshua son of Nun.
verses.after: Moses came and spoke all the words of this song in the people’s hearing, he and Hoshea son of Nun.
verses.tsw_comparator: Moses came and spoke all the words of this song in the hearing of the people, he and Joshua son of Nun.

verses.rationale: Retains the completion and comprehensive audience as the introduction to his final charge.
verses.before: When Moses had finished speaking all these words to all Israel,
verses.after: When Moses had finished speaking all these words to all Israel,
verses.tsw_comparator: When Moses had finished speaking all these words to all Israel,

verses.rationale: Keeps heart reception, testimony, children, and the full instruction linked together.
verses.before: he said to them, “Set your heart on all the words that I testify against you today, which you will command your children to be careful to do, all the words of this instruction.
verses.after: he said to them, “Take to heart all the words I am solemnly declaring to you today. Command your children to faithfully carry out all the words of this instruction.
verses.tsw_comparator: he said to them, “Set your heart on all the words that I testify against you today, which you shall command your children to be careful to do, all the words of this instruction.

verses.rationale: Preserves word/life identity and its promised duration in the land.
verses.before: For it is not an empty word for you, but it is your life, and by this word you will prolong your days upon the ground that you are crossing the Jordan to possess.”
verses.after: This is no empty word for you—it is your life. Through this word you will live long on the ground you are crossing the Jordan to possess.”
verses.tsw_comparator: For it is not an empty word for you, but it is your life, and by this word you will prolong your days upon the ground that you are crossing the Jordan to possess.”

verses.rationale: Keeps same-day timing and the divine speaker of the mountain command.
verses.before: The LORD spoke to Moses on that very day, saying,
verses.after: That same day the LORD spoke to Moses:
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD spoke to Moses on that very day, saying,

verses.rationale: Retains all four geographical names and the distinction between viewing and possessing.
verses.before: “Go up this mountain of Abarim, Mount Nebo, which is in the land of Moab opposite Jericho, and see the land of Canaan that I am giving to the children of Israel as a possession.
verses.after: “Go up into this Abarim range, to Mount Nebo in the land of Moab opposite Jericho, and see the land of Canaan that I am giving the Israelites as their possession.
verses.tsw_comparator: “Go up this mountain of Abarim, Mount Nebo, which is in the land of Moab opposite Jericho, and see the land of Canaan that I am giving to the children of Israel as a possession.

verses.rationale: Preserves the imperative force and repeated gathering-to-people idiom, including Aaron and Hor.
verses.before: You will die on the mountain that you ascend and be gathered to your people, just as Aaron your brother died on Mount Hor and was gathered to his people,
verses.after: Die on the mountain you climb and be gathered to your people, just as your brother Aaron died on Mount Hor and was gathered to his people.
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall die on the mountain that you ascend and be gathered to your people, just as Aaron your brother died on Mount Hor and was gathered to his people,

verses.rationale: Makes the plural address to Moses and Aaron explicit and preserves both named locations and holiness failure.
verses.before: because you acted unfaithfully against me among the children of Israel at the waters of Meribath-Kadesh, in the wilderness of Zin, because you did not treat me as holy among the children of Israel.
verses.after: For both of you broke faith with me among the Israelites at the waters of Meribath-kadesh in the wilderness of Zin. You did not uphold me as holy among the Israelites.
verses.tsw_comparator: because you acted unfaithfully against me in the midst of the children of Israel at the waters of Meribath-Kadesh, in the wilderness of Zin, because you did not treat me as holy in the midst of the children of Israel.

verses.rationale: Keeps seeing versus entering and the continuing gift to Israel.
verses.before: For from a distance you will see the land, but you will not enter there, into the land that I am giving to the children of Israel.”
verses.after: You will see the land from a distance, but you will not enter the land I am giving the Israelites.”
verses.tsw_comparator: For from a distance you shall see the land, but you shall not enter there, into the land that I am giving to the children of Israel.”

verses.rationale: Preserves the title man of God and the blessing’s timing before death.
verses.before: This is the blessing with which Moses, the man of God, blessed the children of Israel before his death.
verses.after: This is the blessing with which Moses, the man of God, blessed the Israelites before his death.
verses.tsw_comparator: This is the blessing with which Moses, the man of God, blessed the children of Israel before his death.

verses.rationale: Follows the pinned holy-myriad wording and recorded two-word read form fiery law, while flagging the obscure final line.
verses.before: He said: “The LORD came from Sinai and dawned upon them from Seir; he shone forth from Mount Paran and came from myriads of holy ones. At his right hand was fiery instruction for them.
verses.after: He said: “The LORD came from Sinai and dawned upon them from Seir. He shone from Mount Paran and came from myriads of holy ones; from his right hand came a fiery law for them.
verses.tsw_comparator: He said: “The LORD came from Sinai and dawned upon them from Seir; he shone forth from Mount Paran and came from myriads of holy ones. At his right hand was fiery instruction for them.

verses.rationale: Retains peoples and his/your shifts; selects bow for the rare verb and distributes the singular receiving action.
verses.before: Indeed, he loves the peoples; all his holy ones are in your hand. They sat down at your feet; each receives from your words.
verses.after: Indeed, he cherishes the peoples; all his holy ones are in your hand. They bow at your feet; each receives your words.
verses.tsw_comparator: Indeed, he loves the peoples; all his holy ones are in your hand. They sat down at your feet; each receives from your words.

verses.rationale: Preserves the community’s us voice within Moses’ blessing instead of rewriting it as I commanded you.
verses.before: Moses commanded us instruction, an inheritance for the assembly of Jacob.
verses.after: Moses commanded us instruction, an inheritance for the assembly of Jacob.
verses.tsw_comparator: Moses commanded us instruction, an inheritance for the assembly of Jacob.

verses.rationale: Keeps the unnamed he and Jeshurun, leaving the king’s identity open in the text.
verses.before: And he became king in Jeshurun when the heads of the people gathered, together with the tribes of Israel.
verses.after: He was king in Jeshurun when the heads of the people gathered, when Israel’s tribes came together.
verses.tsw_comparator: And he became king in Jeshurun when the heads of the people gathered, together with the tribes of Israel.

verses.rationale: Does not insert a second not before few; renders the compact final clause concessively and records the alternative.
verses.before: May Reuben live and not die, though his men be few.
verses.after: May Reuben live and not die, though his men are few.”
verses.tsw_comparator: May Reuben live and not die, though his men be few.

verses.rationale: Keeps Judah’s voice, return to his people, striving hands, and request for divine aid.
verses.before: And this concerning Judah. He said: “Hear, O LORD, the voice of Judah, and bring him to his people. With his hands he contends for himself; be a help against his adversaries.”
verses.after: He said this of Judah: “Hear Judah’s voice, LORD, and bring him to his people. His hands contend for him; be his help against his foes.”
verses.tsw_comparator: And this concerning Judah. He said: “Hear, O LORD, the voice of Judah, and bring him to his people. With his hands he contends for himself; be a help against his adversaries.”

verses.rationale: Preserves Thummim/Urim order and the unnamed faithful man, with testing/contention wordplay noted.
verses.before: Concerning Levi he said: “Your Thummim and your Urim belong to your faithful one, whom you tested at Massah, with whom you contended at the waters of Meribah;
verses.after: Of Levi he said: “Let your Thummim and Urim belong to your faithful man, whom you tested at Massah, with whom you contended at the waters of Meribah.
verses.tsw_comparator: Concerning Levi he said: “Your Thummim and your Urim belong to your faithful one, whom you tested at Massah, with whom you contended at the waters of Meribah;

verses.rationale: Uses the contextual regard sense of not seeing parents, follows read plural sons, and keeps the shift to they.
verses.before: who said of his father and mother, ‘I do not regard them,’ and did not recognize his brothers or acknowledge his sons, for they kept your word and guarded your covenant.
verses.after: He said of his father and mother, ‘I do not regard them.’ He did not acknowledge his brothers or recognize his own sons. For they kept your word and guarded your covenant.
verses.tsw_comparator: who said of his father and mother, ‘I do not regard them,’ and did not recognize his brothers or acknowledge his sons, for they kept your word and guarded your covenant.

verses.rationale: Retains parallel teaching roles and the embodied incense image instead of replacing it with general worship.
verses.before: They will teach your judgments to Jacob and your instruction to Israel. They will put incense before your face and whole burnt offering upon your altar.
verses.after: They will teach your judgments to Jacob and your instruction to Israel. They will place incense before your nostrils and whole offerings on your altar.
verses.tsw_comparator: They shall teach your judgments to Jacob and your instruction to Israel. They shall put incense before your face and whole burnt offering upon your altar.

verses.rationale: Preserves the bodily violence and the repeated rise contrast alongside blessing and acceptance.
verses.before: Bless, O LORD, his strength, and accept the work of his hands. Shatter the loins of people who rise against him and people who hate him, so that they rise no more.”
verses.after: Bless his strength, LORD, and accept the work of his hands. Shatter the loins of those who rise against him, of those who hate him, so they cannot rise again.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Bless, O LORD, his strength, and accept the work of his hands. Shatter the loins of those who rise against him and those who hate him, so that they rise no more.”

verses.rationale: Keeps the intimate protection image and source pronouns without asserting a certain identification of every he/him.
verses.before: Concerning Benjamin he said: “The beloved of the LORD will dwell securely beside him. He shelters him all the day, and between his shoulders he dwells.”
verses.after: Of Benjamin he said: “The LORD’s beloved rests securely beside him. He shelters him all day long, and he dwells between his shoulders.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Concerning Benjamin he said: “The beloved of the LORD shall dwell securely beside him. He shelters him all the day, and between his shoulders he dwells.”

verses.rationale: Preserves heaven/deep pairing and the crouching waters image while beginning the extended blessing list.
verses.before: Concerning Joseph he said: “Blessed by the LORD is his land, with the choice gifts of the heavens, with dew, and with the deep crouching beneath;
verses.after: Of Joseph he said: “May the LORD bless his land with heaven’s precious gifts, with dew, and with the deep crouching below,
verses.tsw_comparator: Concerning Joseph he said: “Blessed by the LORD is his land, with the choice gifts of the heavens, with dew, and with the deep crouching beneath;

verses.rationale: Keeps sun and plural moons rather than silently reducing the latter to a single moon.
verses.before: with the choice produce of the sun and the choice yield of the months;
verses.after: with the precious produce of the sun and the precious yield of the moons,
verses.tsw_comparator: with the choice produce of the sun and the choice yield of the months;

verses.rationale: Preserves both ages and landforms in parallel lines.
verses.before: with the best of the ancient mountains and the choice gifts of the everlasting hills;
verses.after: with the best from ancient mountains and precious gifts from everlasting hills,
verses.tsw_comparator: with the best of the ancient mountains and the choice gifts of the everlasting hills;

verses.rationale: Retains bush-dweller and head/crown imagery without turning set apart into a formal Nazirite vow.
verses.before: with the choice gifts of the earth and its fullness, and the favor of the one who dwelt in the bush. May these come upon the head of Joseph and upon the crown of the one set apart from his brothers.
verses.after: with the precious gifts of the earth and all that fills it, and the favor of the one who dwelt in the bush. Let these come upon Joseph’s head, upon the crown of the one set apart from his brothers.
verses.tsw_comparator: with the choice gifts of the earth and its fullness, and the favor of the one who dwelt in the bush. May these come upon the head of Joseph and upon the crown of the one set apart from his brothers.

verses.rationale: Preserves bull and wild-ox images, goring violence, and the unequal Ephraim/Manasseh numbers.
verses.before: His firstborn bull has majesty, and his horns are the horns of a wild ox. With them he will gore peoples, all of them, to the ends of the earth. They are the ten thousands of Ephraim, and they are the thousands of Manasseh.”
verses.after: His firstborn bull has majesty; his horns are the horns of a wild ox. With them he gores peoples together to the ends of the earth. They are Ephraim’s ten thousands; they are Manasseh’s thousands.”
verses.tsw_comparator: His firstborn bull has majesty, and his horns are the horns of a wild ox. With them he will gore peoples, all of them, to the ends of the earth. They are the ten thousands of Ephraim, and they are the thousands of Manasseh.”

verses.rationale: Keeps Zebulun and Issachar together with their contrasting settings.
verses.before: Concerning Zebulun he said: “Rejoice, Zebulun, in your going out, and Issachar, in your tents.
verses.after: Of Zebulun he said: “Rejoice, Zebulun, in your going out, and Issachar, in your tents.
verses.tsw_comparator: Concerning Zebulun he said: “Rejoice, Zebulun, in your going out, and Issachar, in your tents.

verses.rationale: Preserves the unnamed mountain, righteous sacrifices, and striking suckling-from-seas image.
verses.before: They will call peoples to the mountain; there they will sacrifice righteous sacrifices. For they will draw the abundance of the seas and hidden treasures of the sand.”
verses.after: They will call peoples to the mountain and offer righteous sacrifices there. For they suck the abundance of the seas and the treasures hidden in the sand.”
verses.tsw_comparator: They will call peoples to the mountain; there they will sacrifice righteous sacrifices. For they will draw the abundance of the seas and hidden treasures of the sand.”

verses.rationale: Keeps the blessing’s recipient as Gad’s enlarger and preserves the violent lion image and both body parts.
verses.before: Concerning Gad he said: “Blessed is the one who enlarges Gad. He dwells like a lion and tears arm and crown of head.
verses.after: Of Gad he said: “Blessed is the one who makes room for Gad! He lies down like a lion and tears off an arm, even a scalp.
verses.tsw_comparator: Concerning Gad he said: “Blessed is the one who enlarges Gad. He dwells like a lion and tears arm and crown of head.

verses.rationale: Keeps the obscure ruler’s reserved portion without identifying it as Moses’ grave, and retains the justice claims.
verses.before: He saw the first portion for himself, for there a commander’s portion was reserved. He came with the heads of the people; he carried out the righteousness of the LORD and his judgments with Israel.”
verses.after: He chose the best portion for himself, for there a ruler’s portion was reserved. He came with the heads of the people; he carried out the LORD’s righteousness and his judgments with Israel.”
verses.tsw_comparator: He saw the first portion for himself, for there a commander’s portion was reserved. He came with the heads of the people; he carried out the righteousness of the LORD and his judgments with Israel.”

verses.rationale: Preserves the source’s Bashan location rather than substituting a later settlement.
verses.before: Concerning Dan he said: “Dan is a lion’s cub that leaps out from Bashan.”
verses.after: Of Dan he said: “Dan is a lion’s cub, leaping from Bashan.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Concerning Dan he said: “Dan is a lion’s cub that leaps out from Bashan.”

verses.rationale: Chooses west for the sea/west term while retaining south and noting the geographical alternative.
verses.before: Concerning Naphtali he said: “Naphtali, satisfied with favor and full of the blessing of the LORD, possess the west and the south.”
verses.after: Of Naphtali he said: “Naphtali, satisfied with favor and full of the LORD’s blessing, take possession of the west and the south.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Concerning Naphtali he said: “Naphtali, satisfied with favor and full of the blessing of the LORD, possess the west and the south.”

verses.rationale: Keeps the among-sons reading and the abundance image of a foot dipped in oil.
verses.before: Concerning Asher he said: “Blessed above sons is Asher; may he be favored by his brothers, and may he dip his foot in oil.
verses.after: Of Asher he said: “May Asher be blessed among sons; may he be favored by his brothers and dip his foot in oil.
verses.tsw_comparator: Concerning Asher he said: “Blessed above sons is Asher; may he be favored by his brothers, and may he dip his foot in oil.

verses.rationale: Selects bars and strength for two uncertain terms, retaining both metals and the days comparison.
verses.before: Iron and bronze will be your bars, and as your days, so will your strength be.”
verses.after: May your bars be iron and bronze, and your strength last as long as your days.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Iron and bronze shall be your bars, and as your days, so shall your strength be.”

verses.rationale: Keeps direct address to Jeshurun and the divine sky-rider image.
verses.before: “There is none like the God of Jeshurun, who rides through the heavens to your help and through the clouds in his majesty.
verses.after: “There is no one like God, Jeshurun, riding the heavens to help you, the clouds in his majesty.
verses.tsw_comparator: “There is none like the God of Jeshurun, who rides through the heavens to your help and through the clouds in his majesty.

verses.rationale: Preserves ancient God, dwelling, arms, and the explicit destructive command without conjectural replacement.
verses.before: The eternal God is a dwelling place, and underneath are everlasting arms. He drove out the enemy before you and said, ‘Destroy!’
verses.after: The God of old is your dwelling place; beneath you are everlasting arms. He drove the enemy from before you and said, ‘Destroy!’
verses.tsw_comparator: The eternal God is a dwelling place, and underneath are everlasting arms. He drove out the enemy before you and said, ‘Destroy!’

verses.rationale: Retains the spring-of-Jacob image and the source’s alone term, with agricultural abundance.
verses.before: So Israel dwells securely, the fountain of Jacob alone, in a land of grain and new wine; indeed, his heavens drop dew.
verses.after: Israel dwells securely, the spring of Jacob alone, in a land of grain and new wine, where the heavens drip dew.
verses.tsw_comparator: So Israel dwells securely, the fountain of Jacob alone, in a land of grain and new wine; indeed, his heavens drop dew.

verses.rationale: Preserves shield and sword, enemy submission, and pinned high places rather than substituting backs.
verses.before: Happy are you, Israel! Who is like you, a people saved by the LORD, the shield of your help and the sword of your majesty? Your enemies will cringe before you, and you will tread upon their heights.”
verses.after: Happy are you, Israel! Who is like you, a people saved by the LORD? He is the shield that helps you, the sword of your majesty. Your enemies will cringe before you, and you will tread their high places.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Happy are you, Israel! Who is like you, a people saved by the LORD, the shield of your help and the sword of your majesty? Your enemies will cringe before you, and you will tread upon their heights.”

verses.rationale: Preserves the ascent locations and begins the full geographical panorama without closing the list early.
verses.before: Then Moses went up from the plains of Moab to Mount Nebo, to the top of Pisgah, which is opposite Jericho. And the LORD showed him all the land—Gilead as far as Dan,
verses.after: Moses went up from the plains of Moab to Mount Nebo, to the summit of Pisgah opposite Jericho. The LORD showed him all the land: Gilead as far as Dan,
verses.tsw_comparator: Then Moses went up from the plains of Moab to Mount Nebo, to the top of Pisgah, which is opposite Jericho. And the LORD showed him all the land—Gilead as far as Dan,

verses.rationale: Keeps the four named regions and the sea boundary.
verses.before: all Naphtali, the land of Ephraim and Manasseh, all the land of Judah as far as the western sea,
verses.after: all Naphtali, the land of Ephraim and Manasseh, all the land of Judah as far as the western sea,
verses.tsw_comparator: all Naphtali, the land of Ephraim and Manasseh, all the land of Judah as far as the western sea,

verses.rationale: Preserves Negev, the plain, Jericho’s epithet, and the final Zoar limit.
verses.before: the Negev, and the plain, that is, the valley of Jericho, the city of palm trees, as far as Zoar.
verses.after: the Negev, and the Jordan plain—the valley of Jericho, the city of palms—as far as Zoar.
verses.tsw_comparator: the Negev, and the plain, that is, the valley of Jericho, the city of palm trees, as far as Zoar.

verses.rationale: Keeps all three ancestors, nested promise, and the contrast between seeing and entering.
verses.before: And the LORD said to him, “This is the land of which I swore to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob, saying, ‘I will give it to your offspring.’ I have let you see it with your eyes, but you will not cross over there.”
verses.after: The LORD said to him, “This is the land I swore to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, saying, ‘I will give it to your descendants.’ I have let you see it with your own eyes, but you will not cross over into it.”
verses.tsw_comparator: And the LORD said to him, “This is the land of which I swore to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob, saying, ‘I will give it to your offspring.’ I have let you see it with your eyes, but you shall not cross over there.”

verses.rationale: Renders at the LORD’s mouth as command while retaining servant and death location.
verses.before: So Moses the servant of the LORD died there in the land of Moab, according to the word of the LORD,
verses.after: So Moses, the LORD’s servant, died there in the land of Moab, at the LORD’s command.
verses.tsw_comparator: So Moses the servant of the LORD died there in the land of Moab, according to the word of the LORD,

verses.rationale: Preserves the unnamed burial agent in the Hebrew, explaining the likely divine referent in a note rather than silently fixing it.
verses.before: and he buried him in the valley in the land of Moab opposite Beth-peor, but no one knows the place of his burial to this day.
verses.after: He buried him in the valley in the land of Moab, opposite Beth-peor. To this day no one knows where his grave is.
verses.tsw_comparator: and he buried him in the valley in the land of Moab opposite Beth-peor, but no one knows the place of his burial to this day.

verses.rationale: Keeps the exact age and undiminished sight and vigor, avoiding a contradiction imported into 31:2.
verses.before: Moses was one hundred twenty years old when he died; his eye was not dim, nor had his vigor fled.
verses.after: Moses was a hundred and twenty years old when he died. His eyes had not grown dim, and his vigor had not left him.
verses.tsw_comparator: Moses was one hundred twenty years old when he died; his eye was not dim, nor had his vigor fled.

verses.rationale: Preserves thirty days, location, and the repeated mourning description.
verses.before: And the sons of Israel wept for Moses in the plains of Moab thirty days. Then the days of weeping and mourning for Moses were completed.
verses.after: The Israelites wept for Moses on the plains of Moab for thirty days. Then the days of weeping and mourning for Moses came to an end.
verses.tsw_comparator: And the sons of Israel wept for Moses in the plains of Moab thirty days. Then the days of weeping and mourning for Moses were completed.

verses.rationale: Keeps Joshua’s parentage, wisdom, laying on of hands, and the continuity of command through Moses.
verses.before: Joshua the son of Nun was full of the spirit of wisdom, for Moses had laid his hands on him. So the sons of Israel listened to him and did as the LORD had commanded Moses.
verses.after: Joshua son of Nun was filled with the spirit of wisdom, because Moses had laid his hands on him. The Israelites listened to him and did as the LORD had commanded Moses.
verses.tsw_comparator: And Joshua the son of Nun was full of the spirit of wisdom, for Moses had laid his hands on him. So the sons of Israel listened to him and did as the LORD had commanded Moses.

verses.rationale: Preserves the direction of knowing from the LORD toward Moses and continues the comparison into the final verses. Consistency refinement: Keeps the narrator’s retrospective since and the LORD as the one who knew Moses. Ends a complete sentence before restating the comparison, so the relative clause cannot seem to modify Israel.
verses.before: And there has not arisen a prophet since in Israel like Moses, whom the LORD knew face to face,
verses.after: Since then, no prophet has arisen in Israel like Moses, whom the LORD knew face to face.
verses.tsw_comparator: And there has not arisen a prophet since in Israel like Moses, whom the LORD knew face to face,

consistency_history.prior_after: Never again has a prophet like Moses arisen in Israel, whom the LORD knew face to face,
consistency_history.prior_rationale: Preserves the direction of knowing from the LORD toward Moses and continues the comparison into the final verses.
consistency_history.rationale: Keeps the narrator’s retrospective since and the LORD as the one who knew Moses. Ends a complete sentence before restating the comparison, so the relative clause cannot seem to modify Israel.

verses.rationale: Retains the comprehensive Egyptian recipients and Moses’ commissioned signs within the closing comparison. Consistency refinement: Restates the implicit comparison with a prophet like Moses as an English main clause. Preserves every recipient and the LORD’s commissioning, continuing the final comparison into verse 12.
verses.before: none like him for all the signs and the wonders that the LORD sent him to do in the land of Egypt, to Pharaoh and to all his servants and to all his land,
verses.after: No prophet has matched him in all the signs and wonders the LORD sent him to perform in the land of Egypt against Pharaoh, all his servants, and all his land,
verses.tsw_comparator: none like him for all the signs and the wonders that the LORD sent him to do in the land of Egypt, to Pharaoh and to all his servants and to all his land,

consistency_history.prior_after: with all the signs and wonders the LORD sent him to perform in the land of Egypt against Pharaoh, all his servants, and all his land,
consistency_history.prior_rationale: Retains the comprehensive Egyptian recipients and Moses’ commissioned signs within the closing comparison.
consistency_history.rationale: Restates the implicit comparison with a prophet like Moses as an English main clause. Preserves every recipient and the LORD’s commissioning, continuing the final comparison into verse 12.

verses.rationale: Keeps mighty hand and great terror as the book’s final images and all Israel as their witnesses. Consistency refinement: Completes the comparison begun in verse 11 and removes the awkward all-the-mighty-hand construction. The hand image, great terror, named Moses, and all-Israel witnesses remain intact.
verses.before: and for all the mighty hand and all the great fear that Moses did in the sight of all Israel.
verses.after: or in the mighty hand and all the great terror Moses displayed before the eyes of all Israel.
verses.tsw_comparator: and for all the mighty hand and all the great fear that Moses did in the sight of all Israel.

consistency_history.prior_after: and with all the mighty hand and all the great terror Moses displayed before the eyes of all Israel.
consistency_history.prior_rationale: Keeps mighty hand and great terror as the book’s final images and all Israel as their witnesses.
consistency_history.rationale: Completes the comparison begun in verse 11 and removes the awkward all-the-mighty-hand construction. The hand image, great terror, named Moses, and all-Israel witnesses remain intact.
